newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB maintains buy rating on Danubius.
newsitem.headline: CSFB maintains buy rating on Danubius.

text.p: CS First Boston has maintained its buy recommendation on Danubius Hotels shares following the green light on Wednesday for its acquisition of hotel chain Hungaria Szalloda Rt.

"The deal appears highly beneficial to Danubius," CS First Boston said in its latest study on Danubius. "We expect significant efficiency gains to be realised, despite the formal separation of the compnies."
The author of the report, Spender Jakab, said that CSFB was boosting its target price for the stock by 21.3 percent.
Hungary's Competition Agency approved earlier this week Danubius' 8.125 billion forint purchase of 85 percent of Hungaria.

The state privatisation agency APV Rt agreed to the deal in August on condition that the Competition Agency established that the total market share of the merged hotel chains did not exceed the maximum permitted 30 percent.
The conditions of the tender required Danubius to seek a stock market flotation of a least 50 percent of Hungaria shares within a year.
Jakab predicted 50 percent of the stock could be floated in January 1998, at an earnings multiple of roughly 10 times and that the group will experience a roughly 60 percent earnings growth in 1997.
As a result, CFSB's earnings per share forecast has been downgraded by 29.2 percent for 1997 but boosted for 1998 and 1999 by 71 percent and 1.3 percent respectively.
